name: Fernpass
kurzbeschreibung: The Fern Pass at 1,216 metres is a storied alpine mountain pass between Reutte and Imst, celebrated for its Zugspitze panoramas, Lake Blindsee, and Roman history.
preis: Mountain pass road and scenic viewing points freely accessible (toll-free)
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round 24/7 (winter tires or snow chains required in snowy conditions)
beschreibung:
Überblick

The storied Fern Pass (Fernpass) crests at an elevation of 1,216 metres in the Tyrolean Alps, connecting the Außerfern district around Reutte with the Upper Inn Valley near Imst. As one of the most historically significant and visually dramatic mountain crossings in the Eastern Alps, the pass was engineered over two millennia ago by the Romans as part of the transalpine trade route Via Claudia Augusta. Created by a colossal prehistoric rockslide approximately 4,000 years ago, nature sculpted a rugged alpine wonderland studded with pine forests and crystal-clear emerald lakes, including Lake Blindsee, Lake Mittersee, and romantic Lake Fernsteinsee. From the pass summit and panoramic rest terraces, travelers enjoy sweeping views of the mighty Zugspitze massif and the jagged limestone pinnacles of the Lechtal Alps. Today, the toll-free highway is both a vital transport artery and a cherished leisure haven for hikers, road-trippers, and cyclists.

Route & Anforderungen

Crossing the mountain pass along federal highway B179 is open year-round to all standard passenger vehicles, motorhomes, and motorcycles, boasting well-maintained asphalt and engineered switchbacks with moderate gradients. Spacious viewing balconies and rest stops at the mountain crest invite drivers to pause and take photographs. While a scenic driving stop requires merely 30 to 60 minutes, outdoor lovers can spend two to three hours exploring the terrain along the original stone-paved Roman roads descending to turquoise Lake Blindsee or strolling around Lake Fernsteinsee and its historic castle hotel. Flat casual shoes are sufficient for roadside viewpoints, whereas sturdy hiking shoes with lugged soles are advised for walking along the lakeside nature trails.

Besuch & Anreise

The Fernpass is situated directly along highway B179, linking Bavaria and the German border toll-free with Western Austria and Italy. Generous free parking spaces are provided at the pass summit next to roadside eateries as well as at scenic roadside lookouts. By public transit, regional VVT express bus lines operate frequent year-round services connecting Reutte in Tirol railway station with Imst-Pitztal station across the mountain pass.

Tipps

Do not pass by the famous 'Zugspitzblick' viewpoint located just north of the pass summit: from the cliffside railing, one gazes directly down into the turquoise waters of Lake Blindsee with the sheer wall of the Zugspitze rising majestically in the background. Pair your visit with a brief stroll along the wooded shores of Lake Fernsteinsee.
